sources.entry: Matchering - Automated music mastering (alternative to LANDR, eMastered and MajorDecibel). GPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Matchering is an open-source Python library, web app, and ComfyUI node that masters a target audio track to match the RMS, frequency response, peak amplitude and stereo width of a reference track.
summary.what_it_does: You supply two audio files: a TARGET track to be mastered and a REFERENCE track whose sound you want to match. The algorithm analyzes both and outputs a mastered version of the target with the same RMS, frequency response, peak amplitude and stereo width as the reference. The README says it is available as a containerized web application (Docker image), a Python package on PyPI, a ComfyUI node, and as part of the UVR5 Desktop App. The Python library can save output as 16-bit or 24-bit PCM WAV files. Its limiter is the project's own Hyrax brickwall limiter. The README also links to a separate command-line wrapper, matchering-cli.
use_cases: Master a home-recorded song to sound like a reference track
Make all tracks on an album sound consistent
Batch-master audio from a Python script or pipeline
Run an AI mastering service via a Docker container
Match the loudness and tonal balance of one song to another
how_to_run: Desktop: in UVR5 Desktop App, choose Process Method > Audio Tools & Choose Audio Tool > Matchering
Python library (Linux/macOS): python3 -m pip install -U matchering
Python library (Windows): python -m pip install -U matchering
Optional MP3 support: install FFmpeg (for example sudo apt -y install ffmpeg on Ubuntu)
Linux prerequisite: sudo apt update && sudo apt -y install libsndfile1
notable: Reference-based mastering: the target is shaped to match a reference track's RMS, frequency response, peak and stereo width
Multiple entry points: Python library, Docker web app, ComfyUI node, and UVR5 desktop app
Rewritten in Python 3 from the earlier MATLAB version, with an open-source Hyrax limiter
Can output 16-bit or 24-bit PCM WAV files
caveats: Python library needs at least 4 GB RAM and Python 3.8.0 or higher
Linux users must install libsndfile through their package manager; MP3 loading needs the optional FFmpeg install
Result quality depends on choosing a suitable reference track, according to the README's cited review
keywords: make my track sound like a reference
